prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1135; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision reported by the insured's driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant reports neck pain and has not retained a lawyer.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the accident happened as described, and the other driver's account matches. Photos of the rear bumper are on file.

Entry 3: Police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Claimant gave a statement that is consistent with the initial report.

Entry 4: Reviewed the vehicle's prior repair history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 5: Claimant was seen at urgent care the same day and diagnosed with whiplash. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type.

Entry 6: Claimant described the same account of the collision in every conversation so far. No changes to the timeline or sequence have come up.

Entry 7: Claimant's records show a minor strain in the same neck area several years ago, which healed fully according to the prior provider notes.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested a updated treatment plan and records from the treating clinic.

Entry 9: Clinic records are received. Physical therapy visits continue, and the notes describe gradual improvement with some ongoing stiffness.

Entry 10: Reviewed the damage estimate against the photos. It is not clear yet whether all of the claimed damage came from this impact, so the question is open.

Entry 11: Sent a request to the medical reviewer to assess how much of the current treatment relates to this collision, given the earlier strain.

Entry 12: File remains open pending the medical reviewer's opinion on causation and the final treatment update from the clinic.
